title: Consensus-gated Multi-Agent Neural Architecture Search for Seismic Fault Segmentation
authors: Baig, S.; Mustafa, A.
task: neural architecture search for seismic fault segmentation under a tight labelled-data and parameter budget
agentic_techniques: multi-agent-debate; role-specialisation; code-execution; self-reflection; memory; guardrails-validation
tools_used: code authoring and cross-review of complete PyTorch network implementations; an automated pre-training validator (AST parsing, instantiation, forward and backward pass at batch size 1 on three section shapes, spatial-dimension and 450,000-parameter checks); a train-and-score loop on a single laptop GPU via the MPS backend; a JSON search history, ban list and per-provider token logger
evaluation_method: an identical-protocol benchmark retraining every architecture including all baselines on all 100 training sections for 60 epochs with the same loss and optimizer, evaluated on the full test volume, reporting F1, IoU, precision, recall and PR-AUC; during search, candidates were scored as the mean of three trials on a five-section proxy with keep-or-revert gating
baseline: published-capacity U-Net (31.04M), U-Net (1.81M), DeepLabV3-ResNet50 (39.63M), Attention U-Net (1.83M), and a 1.49M-parameter reference baseline within the search lineage
reported_result: the discovered network is 'simultaneously the smallest and the most accurate model: F1 0.578 and IoU 0.406 at 0.43M parameters', beating the published-capacity U-Net by +0.094 F1 at 73x fewer parameters
maturity_claimed: for specialized dense-prediction tasks, reasoned code-level architecture search is now cheaper than scaling, and multi-model debate is an effective quality gate for scarce training compute
author_stated_limitations: Authors report a cautionary finding that 'optimizing recall alone silently discards the best F1 designs', noting an earlier recall-driven search 'had kept a worse model and reverted its genuinely best design'; they state quantitative metrics are often insufficient for fault segmentation given incomplete and uncertain ground-truth labels, so the pipeline can discard valid architectures on minor metric regressions, and propose a future agent to judge visual quality; they note published Thebe results are not directly comparable because they use tolerance-based OIS/ODS matching on different splits, and that one debate run was aborted on a provider transport failure.

authors: Song, Z.; Xiang, Z.; Yang, J.; et al.
task: document-level extraction of structured entity-attribute records, with sentence- and page-level evidence tracing, from ultra-long legacy geoscience literature

base_model: GeoGPT-R1-Preview (based on Qwen2.5-72B) as Orchestrator and for attribute extraction; DeepSeek-V3 for entity extraction; bge-base-en-v1.5 and BGE-M3 embeddings; bce-reranker-base_v1 and BGE-reranker-large rerankers; temperature 0.0, no model weights updated

evaluation_method: the unedited output was archived before expert review, domain experts then corrected, removed and added records to build an expert-adjudicated reference, and entity- and attribute-level recall/precision/F1 were computed against it. Palaeontology was exhaustive across all 55 volumes with no record-level subsampling (32,277 entities, 14 attributes each); palaeomagnetism used 13 of 567 articles fully annotated and selected before metric calculation (316 entities, 10 attributes); geochemistry used 7 documents (127 entities, 10 variables) against the public Ball (2024) GFZ/GEOROC dataset. End-to-end turnaround per volume was compared against a fully manual extraction experiment.
baseline: a fully manual extraction experiment on one volume by four annotators (45 calendar days); expert-adjudicated reference datasets as ground truth; no competing automated extraction system
reported_result: average F1 approximately 0.90 for entities and 0.91 for attributes, with per-volume efficiency approximately sixfold better than the manual baseline (7 calendar days per volume against 45); a released database of 32,277 fossil taxonomic entities and 451,878 attributes built in 53 person-days; palaeomagnetism entity precision 0.93 / recall 0.96 and attribute precision 0.81 / recall 0.77; geochemistry entity F1 0.81 and attribute F1 0.51 (recall 0.35, precision 0.93)

author_stated_limitations: Authors state the two-stage strategy 'introduces potential error propagation' with 'cascading errors in the output structure' when entities are missed or merged; that conservative paragraph filtering 'can also reduce recall when genuinely relevant fossil descriptions are incomplete or expressed without these cues'; that chunking and RAG on extremely long documents 'inevitably introduces a trade-off between efficiency and recall', consistent with lost-in-the-middle findings; that cross-page discontinuity can split a description so 'the latter part of the split description can be excluded'; that 'fully understanding table semantics remains difficult' for cross-page tables, merged cells and footnotes; that performance 'is influenced by the underlying OCR and layout analysis algorithms', worse for older scans; and that expert verification throughput 'represents a practical bottleneck'.
